questions.question_text:
A printing press bought for $\$54\,000$ is depreciated by the straight-line method at $\$6200$ per year.
What is its salvage value after $5$ years?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation $6200 \times 5$ instead of the value left.
Subtracted only one year of depreciation instead of five.
Used $n = 4$ instead of $n = 5$ in $S = V_{0} - Dn$.

questions.question_text:
A machine costs $\$19\,500$. It is written down to zero over $6$ years using the straight-line method.
What is the annual depreciation amount?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation over all six years instead of the annual amount.
Multiplied the purchase price by six instead of dividing by six.
Divided by five years instead of six.

questions.question_text:
A van costs $\$43\,000$. Using straight-line depreciation, it loses $10\%$ of its purchase price each year.
After how many years will its value be $\$17\,200$?

options.why: Divided the purchase price by the annual depreciation amount, giving the time to reach zero.
Divided the salvage value by the annual depreciation amount instead of dividing the value lost.
Added the purchase price and salvage value before dividing by the annual depreciation amount.

questions.question_text:
An oven costs $\$11\,400$. It depreciates by $\$1275$ each year using the straight-line method.
What is its salvage value after $4$ years?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation instead of subtracting it from the purchase price.
Subtracted only one year of depreciation.
Subtracted three years of depreciation instead of four.

questions.question_text:
An asset costs $\$31\,000$. It depreciates by $\$3250$ each year using the straight-line method.
What is its salvage value after $5$ years?

options.why: Gave the total depreciation instead of the value remaining.
Subtracted only one year of depreciation.
Subtracted four years of depreciation instead of five.

questions.question_text:
Equipment costs $\$64\,000$. Using straight-line depreciation, it loses $9\%$ of its purchase price each year.
After how many years will its value be $\$23\,680$?

options.why: Used one annual depreciation amount instead of the total loss of $\$40\,320$.
Counted six annual losses, which leaves $\$29\,440$ rather than $\$23\,680$.
Counted eight annual losses, which leaves $\$17\,920$ rather than $\$23\,680$.
Gave the total fall over six years instead of dividing by six.
Gave the value remaining after six years instead of the annual loss.
Gave the initial value instead of the annual loss.

questions.solution_text:
The value falls from $\$40\,000$ to $\$10\,000$ over $6$ years.
$D=\dfrac{40000-10000}{6}$
$=30000\div6$
$=\$5000$ per year.

questions.question_text:
A machine costs $\$45\,000$. Using straight-line depreciation, it loses $6\%$ of its purchase price each year.
After how many years will its value be $\$28\,800$?

options.why: Counted five annual losses, leaving $\$31\,500$ instead of $\$28\,800$.
Counted seven annual losses, leaving $\$26\,100$ instead of $\$28\,800$.
Used just one annual loss of $\$2700$ instead of the total loss of $\$16\,200$.

questions.question_text:
A boat costs $\$88\,000$. It depreciates by $\$9500$ per year using the straight-line method for the first $4$ years. It then depreciates at $20\%$ per annum using the declining-balance method.
What is its value $10$ years after purchase, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Applied declining-balance depreciation for four years instead of the remaining six.
Stopped after the straight-line stage at the end of year four.
Gave the total depreciation instead of the final value.
